title: No fake testimonials or false claims

sources.claim: The FTC Trade Regulation Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials took effect on October 21, 2024. It bans fake reviews and testimonials (including AI-generated ones that misrepresent real experiences) and bans incentives conditioned on a review expressing a particular sentiment; asking for honest reviews, even with an incentive not tied to sentiment, is a different case. The course teaches the principle, not the penalty amounts.

sections.skill: Avoid fake testimonials and unsupported claims made with AI

questions.domain: Foundation 12: AI as a practical helper
questions.prompt: Which use of AI is deceptive?

choices.text: Fixing grammar in a real review with permission

questions.intro: AI makes it easy to create text and images, which makes it easy to deceive by accident or on purpose. Never use AI to invent customer testimonials or reviews, create fake "before and after" photos, imply endorsements that did not happen, or make claims you cannot support, such as "clinically proven" or "number one in the state." The FTC treats fake reviews and testimonials as deceptive. Use AI to draft honest descriptions of what your product actually does, and label AI-generated images where it would affect a buyer's decision.

sections.skill: A photo filter on a used-car ad

questions.domain: Foundation 12: AI as a practical helper
questions.prompt: Editing dents out of a car photo is what?
questions.intro: Imagine a used-car ad where the seller edits out the dents and rust. Buyers drive over, see the real car and feel cheated. AI can make that kind of edit in seconds. The rule stays the same as before AI: show the product as it really is and say only what you can back up.
